mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of FEDFUNDS-tightening triggers over a 5-year sample.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes where GDPC1 falls by 2% or more.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate margins, and thus predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly different from zero in more than 70% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average by more than 3% for three consecutive months indicates supply-side stress, which typically precedes negative equity returns over the next 20 trading days due to earnings pressure.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of triggered INDPRO contraction episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (CPI) above their respective 12-month averages by at least 1% signals a dual tightening in monetary and price pressures, which increases recession risk and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of dual-tightening triggers over a 10-year sample.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive co-movement between personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth) and housing starts (HOUST) above their respective 6-month averages signals robust household demand expansion, which predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly above zero in more than 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate below 5% for four consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which historically precedes monetary tightening and negative equity valuations, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent year-over-year increase in real retail sales (RSAFS) above 4% signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts earnings expectations and predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly above zero in more than 70% of triggered RSAFS episodes.
